title: Pipette dye into three wells of water
instruction: Use the transfer pipette to dilute the dark stock by half in each well. The stock is in the right-hand well nearest you, and wells 1, 2 and 3 run away from you along the left-hand row, each holding water. Move one pipetteful from the stock into well 1, then one from well 1 into well 2, then one from well 2 into well 3. Then stand the empty pipette back in its holder and let go.
context: Why: Diluting a liquid step by step is how labs make standards, dose ranges and countable samples, and is among the first bench skills technicians learn (American Society for Microbiology, Serial Dilution Protocols, 2016). Each well is made from the one before, and a used pipette back in an earlier well contaminates it. Done by: biological technicians (O*NET 19-4021); medical and clinical laboratory technicians (O*NET 29-2012).
setup: Positions are centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Magnetic stirrer: a 2mag MIXdrive 6 MTP, the stainless steel stirrer made for six-well plates, 14 x 10.2 x 2.6 cm, 1.3 kg, with six stirring points 3.9 cm apart in two rows of three, one under each well. It is taped down with its long side along x, centred at x 24.4, y 16.05. Its control unit sits off the table, with the cable led away from the arms. It is switched on at a low speed (about 300 rpm, no vortex) before the trial and runs throughout. Plate: a Corning 3516 clear polystyrene six-well plate, lid off, 12.8 x 8.6 x 2 cm, wells 34.8 mm across and 17.4 mm deep, about 3.9 cm apart, about 40 g (not weighed), sitting on the stirrer with a well over each point, taped at its edges. The left-hand row (y 18) is wells 1, 2 and 3 at x 20.5, 24.4 and 28.3: each holds 3.4 mL of clean water and a white PTFE micro stir bar, 5 x 2 mm (Bel-Art Spinbar F37119-0005). The right-hand row (y 14.1) holds the stock in its nearest well (x 20.5): 6.8 mL of blue dye solution (0.25 mL of McCormick blue liquid food colour in 100 mL of water: plainly blue, not black, in a 10 mm cuvette); its other two wells are empty. Pipette holder: a grey PVC square collar, 2.2 cm across inside, 3 mm walls, 5 cm tall, about 20 g, taped down at x 24, y 24. Transfer pipette: a Globe Scientific 137010 large-bulb LDPE transfer pipette, 15 cm long, about 3 g (not weighed), bulb draw 3.4 mL (one full squeeze and release is one pipetteful): a white squeeze bulb (squeeze faces 2.8 cm apart, pointing to the robot's left and right; 2 cm deep; 3 cm tall) on a 12 cm stem 0.8 cm thick, standing tip down in the holder. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored at the end, with the stirrer switched off and the liquid settled, after a top photo for the record. A well is right when it holds between 2.55 and 7.65 mL (one or two pipettefuls), read to the nearest mark of a clean 10 mL graduated syringe that draws up its whole contents (more than fits is over) and its strength is its target: well 1 half the stock, well 2 a quarter, well 3 an eighth. Strength: 1 mL of it in a clean standard 10 mm plastic cuvette, photographed side-on on a white light box beside reference cuvettes made by hand from the same stock at neat, half, quarter, eighth and sixteenth strength; it is right if its closest reference is its target, with boundary cuvettes at 0.707, 0.354, 0.177 and 0.088 of the stock's strength to settle close calls. Wells are read in order, 1 to 3, after the stock well's remaining volume is read the same way (2.55 mL or more must be left) (sim: dye fraction within a factor of 1.41 of the target). Each well must be made only from the one before it: well 1 from the stock, well 2 from well 1, well 3 from well 2 (video). The stirrer needs time to mix: a well that gets liquid drawn from the previous well less than 15 s after liquid from another well last landed there isn't right (sim; on a real bench its colour shows it); squeezing a draw back into its own well spoils nothing, and counts as mixing that well when at least three-quarters of a pipetteful goes back. Wells count in order: 0 if well 1 isn't right, 0.3 for well 1, 0.6 for wells 1 and 2, 0.9 for all three, and 1.0 if the pipette also stands empty in its holder (tip inside the collar, under 2 cm above the table, leaning under 20 degrees) and has been let go: no gripper touching any part of it, and still (moving under 2 cm/s) for 1 s (video). 0 if more than one and a quarter pipettefuls (4.25 mL) were taken out of the stock, net of any squeezed back into it (on a bench: less than 2.55 mL left in the stock well), or if liquid from any other well was squeezed into the stock, or if, after the first draw from the stock, the tip went back into an earlier well's liquid after entering a later one, or liquid was carried back to an earlier well (video). Liquid squeezed out anywhere but over a well, or from more than 3 cm over a well's rim (side video; it still lands in that well, and counts there), caps the score at 0.5. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Switch the stirrer off for the end photo. Empty and rinse the plate's wells, leaving a stir bar in each of wells 1-3; refill the stock well with 6.8 mL of the same dye solution and wells 1-3 with 3.4 mL of water each; switch the stirrer back on at the same speed; empty the pipette and stand it back in its holder, squeeze faces left and right. Scoring kit, kept off the table: clean 10 mL graduated syringes and standard 10 mm cuvettes (one of each per well), a white light box, and five reference cuvettes made by hand from the same stock at neat, half, quarter, eighth and sixteenth strength, plus boundary cuvettes at 0.707, 0.354, 0.177 and 0.088. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No liquids: volumes and dye are tracked per well in Python. A release under the liquid draws what lies above the tip, up to one 3.4 mL pipetteful (the real bulb's draw); a full squeeze empties it. Mixing is computed at once, but colour settles over 15 s and a draw within 15 s of liquid landing counts as unmixed. Stir bars aren't drawn. Wells are eight-sided, the plate opaque with no top deck; water shows pale blue. The bulb is square; the pipette weighs 38 g.
